pharm: Centrally-acting analgesic & antipyretic; weak peripheral anti-inflammatory
quick: Analgesic of choice; lowest effective dose
Total daily dose; LFTs if high-dose/risk
summary: Centrally-acting non-opioid analgesic and antipyretic for mild-moderate pain and fever, well tolerated at therapeutic doses but hepatotoxic in overdose; preferred in pregnancy and when NSAIDs are unsuitable.
indications: Mild-moderate pain (headache, myalgia, arthralgia, dysmenorrhea, dental)
Adjunct in moderate-severe pain with opioids

dosage.d: 500-1000 mg every 4-6 h PRN; max 4000 mg/24h
dosage.n: Cap at 3000 mg/day for OTC self-care; 2000-3000 mg/day with chronic alcohol/hepatic risk
Do not exceed 10 days (pain) or 3 days (fever) without doctor

dosage.d: 10-15 mg/kg/dose every 4-6 h; max 5 doses/24h; max 75 mg/kg/day
1000 mg every 6 h or 650 mg every 4 h; max 4000 mg/day

admin: May be taken with or without food
Oral: swallow with water; do not exceed labeled daily maximum
IV: administer as recommended infusion per product instructions
moa: Centrally-acting analgesic and antipyretic; inhibits central prostaglandin synthesis and acts on hypothalamic heat-regulating center; weak peripheral anti-inflammatory activity.

absolute: Severe hepatic impairment / severe active liver disease
monitor: Liver function with high dose or risk factors

preg: Analgesic/antipyretic of choice in pregnancy; use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
lact: Compatible; excreted in small amounts in breast milk and considered safe.
renal: Caution; severe impairment (CrCl<30) - increase dosing interval to every 6-8 h.
hepatic: Caution/reduce dose; contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment or active liver disease; max 2000-3000 mg/day in mild-moderate impairment or alcoholism.

major: Warfarin - prolonged high-dose use enhances INR and bleeding risk
moderate: CYP enzyme inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampin, isoniazid) - increase hepatotoxic metabolite risk
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false readings on glucose meters (rare); interferes with some uric acid and glucose assays

monitoring: Total daily dose across all products
LFTs in chronic high-dose use or with risk factors
In overdose: serum acetaminophen level (Rumack-Matthew nomogram), LFTs, INR
counsel: Check all OTC and combination products for acetaminophen to avoid duplication
Seek care if overdose suspected, even if feeling well
pearls: Antidote is N-acetylcysteine (NAC), most effective within 8-10 h of overdose
Toxic metabolite NAPQI is detoxified by glutathione
Preferred analgesic in pregnancy and when NSAIDs cannot be used
Little or no anti-platelet, GI, or renal NSAID effects
Toxicity threshold ~150 mg/kg or 7.5-10 g single ingestion
missed: PRN drug - take when needed; skip if near next dose; never double to exceed daily maximum.
overdose: Hepatotoxicity is the main danger. Phases: (1) 0-24h nausea/vomiting/malaise, (2) 24-72h RUQ pain and rising LFTs, (3) 72-96h peak hepatotoxicity/possible liver failure, (4) recovery. Treat with NAC; measure 4-hour post-ingestion level on Rumack-Matthew nomogram; give activated charcoal if early.
